cards.text: Paul is still writing to the church in Corinth. He just asked them, aren't they supposed to judge those inside the church? Now he's heard that when one believer has a grievance against another, he goes to law before the unrighteous, and friend, Paul is HOT about it.

cards.question: Instead of the unrighteous, who does Paul say a believer with a grievance should bring it to?

cards.text: Then Paul starts a question with "Do you not know". He does that three times in this passage, and when Paul opens with those words, friend, BUCKLE UP.

cards.question: Paul tells the Corinthians that the saints will judge the world.
If the Corinthians are going to judge the world, Paul asks, aren't they competent to judge ___ cases?

cards.text: You're gonna judge the WORLD, and you can't settle a little dispute at church? That's like running a whole bakery and calling for help to set the oven timer.

cards.question: Paul goes even bigger than judging the world. Who does he say believers will judge?

cards.text: ANGELS. Then Paul says, "How much more the things of this life!" So why hand everyday matters to judges with no standing in the church, he asks, and he says it to their shame.

cards.question: Paul asks the church in Corinth if they're really missing something. What is it?

answers.text: Someone wise enough to settle it between brothers
Enough money to pay the court fees
A building big enough to hold trials

cards.text: Instead, one brother takes another brother to court. That's like two brothers arguing over the last cookie in the box and hiring a JUDGE to split it.

cards.question: Paul says one brother goes to law against another, and this in front of ___!
Paul says just having lawsuits among them means the Corinthians are thoroughly ___ already.
Instead of suing, Paul asks the Corinthians why they won't do something hard. What is it?

answers.text: Take it to a higher court
Ask Paul to come and decide

cards.text: Then Paul asks, "Why not rather be cheated?" Whew. That one lands like a full tray of cookies on your toe. And he's not done, because the next line flips the whole thing around.

cards.question: Instead of being willing to be wronged, what does Paul say the Corinthians are doing?

answers.text: Cheating and wronging their own brothers
Forgiving and forgetting way too fast
Keeping quiet and staying far away

cards.question: In his third "Do you not know" question, Paul says the wicked will still inherit the kingdom of God.

cards.text: Don't be deceived, Paul says. Then he lists who won't inherit the kingdom of God: the sexually immoral, idolaters, adulterers, men who submit to or perform homosexual acts, thieves, the greedy, drunkards, verbal abusers and swindlers.

cards.question: Paul says some of the Corinthians used to be the kinds of people on that list.
Paul doesn't leave the Corinthians stuck on that list. What does he say happened to them?

answers.text: They were washed and sanctified and justified
They were warned and given time to change
They were sent away from the church

cards.question: Paul says the Corinthians were washed in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by whom?

findings.problem: The card says Paul 'just asked them, aren't they supposed to judge those inside the church?' That fact comes from 1 Corinthians 5:12, which is outside this passage. The card gives no reference for it, and its citation covers only 1 Corinthians 6:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card says Paul opens a question with "Do you not know" three times in this passage. That draws on 6:2, 6:3 and 6:9, but the card cites only 1 Corinthians 6:2.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This card only restates 6:2, which cards 4 and 5 already covered, and adds a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward. The joke should ride along on a card that tells new passage content.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The card packs in more than two beats: the 'ANGELS' reaction and the 6:3 quote, the 6:4 question about appointing judges of no standing, and the 6:5 'to your shame' line.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The question says 'the kinds of people on that list.' That points back to the list on card 17, which is no longer on screen. The question should say what the list is, such as the people Paul says won't inherit the kingdom of God.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question says 'stuck on that list,' which points back to card 17's list. That card is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'washed and sanctified and justified,' uses biblical and theological wording. The wrong answers, 'warned and given time to change' and 'sent away from the church,' use plain everyday wording. That makes the right answer stand out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
